# Remirror Phase 4 — Daily Brief

**Goal:** ship an end-of-day Markdown reflection, generated by Claude using the local data Phase 2a already collects, surfaced in a new Brief tab.

**Spec date:** 2026-05-27
**Operating frame:** [CRYSTALLIZED-CONTEXT-adhd-design-frame.md](./CRYSTALLIZED-CONTEXT-adhd-design-frame.md)
**Expert consult:** Dr. Casey Mercer (ADHD performance coach), 2026-05-27. Synthesis applied throughout.
**Tag target:** v0.3.0

---

## 1. What it is

A written, Claude-generated end-of-day reflection that turns Phase 2a's structured data (sessions, calendar, adherence, project breakdown, work hours, goal) into prose. Five sections with a specific narrative arc designed for the ADHD user who already knows what they did and didn't do, and needs honest data delivered without shame.

The brief lives in a new **Brief tab**. Past briefs are date-keyed below today's. Every brief is locally stored (SQLite) — only the generation step itself touches the Anthropic API.

---

## 2. When the brief fires (v1: manual only)

**Manual generation is the only trigger in v1.** A "Generate today's brief" button on the Brief tab triggers a streamed call to Claude. The button is disabled while a generation is in flight.

**Auto-fire is deliberately not shipped in v1.** Rationale (from Mercer): "Auto-fire on a day-shape you don't yet understand is how you ship a notification that lands during a 9pm depressive spiral. Ship the manual button, watch 30 days of when the founder actually opens it, then design the trigger from real data."

The auto-fire trigger is reserved for v0.4.x once real usage data exists. The codebase MUST NOT include partial auto-fire scaffolding (no `lastBriefAt` timestamps tied to triggers, no cron-like scheduler). Keep the surface small.

---

## 3. Regeneration policy (cap = 2 per day)

The user can regenerate today's brief at most **2 times** after the initial generation. After the 2nd regen, the button disables and a quiet line appears:

> This is the brief. Sit with it.

The cap exists because unlimited regens become a slot machine for the user's inner critic — they will grind until Claude flatters them, which destroys the truth-led frame.

**Per-day generation count is stored** in the `daily_briefs` row's `generation_count` column. Each call (initial + regens) increments it. Tomorrow resets (different date key).

---

## 4. Output structure — five sections + structured tail

Claude emits a single Markdown response with these five sections in order, separated by `## ` headings. After the last section, a code-fenced JSON block contains a compact structured tail used by Phase 5 weekly mirror.

### 4.1 Section schema (exact heading text)

```
## Truth headline
<inline copy: "X focused. Y elsewhere. Longest: Z.">

## Today's story
<2-3 short paragraphs. Narrative. When you started, what you returned to, where you went elsewhere, what you touched.>

## What held
<1-2 sentences naming the specific block / kept event / pattern that actually showed up. Direct, no banned vocab.>

## What fragmented
<1-2 sentences naming the specific switching pattern or partial-event. Mechanism only, no verdict. See §5 for the system prompt language.>

## Tomorrow's first 90
<Concrete: start time, single target, supporting calendar events (if any), competing calendar events (if any). Format: "HH:MM-HH:MM on <target>, before <competing event>." Or "After your <supporting event>, <HH:MM-HH:MM> on <target>.">
```

### 4.2 Structured tail (machine-parsed)

```json
{
  "day_shape": "diffuse" | "anchored" | "fragmented_bursts" | "stretched_focus" | "rest",
  "dominant_fragmentation_pattern": "morning_drift" | "afternoon_slip" | "calendar_collision" | "context_thrash" | "none",
  "tomorrow_first_90": {
    "start_local": "HH:MM",
    "target": "<short project label or task name>",
    "supporting_event_id": "<calendar event id or null>",
    "competing_event_id": "<calendar event id or null>"
  }
}
```

The structured tail is REQUIRED. If Claude omits it or it fails to parse, the brief regenerates (consuming one regen attempt). After 3 parse failures, the brief is stored with `structured_tail = NULL` and a warning is logged.

### 4.3 Bad-day exemplar (locked acceptance test)

This is the calibration target. On a day with 12 minutes focused, 4 hours elsewhere, no kept events, no goal progress, the generated brief must match the **shape** (not exact words) of this example:

```markdown
## Truth headline
12 minutes focused. 4 hours 8 minutes elsewhere. Longest stretch: 12 min on Oracle at 2:14pm.

## Today's story
Today was diffuse. The Oracle dashboard got 12 minutes; the Jackie call and the 10am planning block did not start. Most of the day moved through Twitter, Slack, and the inbox in stretches of 4-9 minutes. There was no anchor block.

## What held
The 2:14pm Oracle attempt was the only stretch where attention landed on the commitment. It was short, and it was real.

## What fragmented
The morning never had a starting block. The first 90 minutes after wake went to inbox and Twitter in alternating 6-minute windows, and the day's shape followed from there.

## Tomorrow's first 90
9:00-10:30 on the Oracle dashboard, before the inbox opens. One target, one window, before anything else gets a vote.
```

The acceptance test for §10's banned-vocab linter MUST scan this example and produce zero violations. Tests in `tests/copy/brief-bad-day.test.ts` verify the linter against this exemplar.

---

## 5. System prompt (canonical text)

The system prompt is versioned. v1.0 reads:

```
You are the voice of Remirror, a desktop app that mirrors a user's actual day back to them so they can reflect honestly. You are not their therapist; you are their coach. You have already seen the data. You are not interpreting it for them — you are naming what happened in language that respects their intelligence.

You will receive a JSON payload describing today's recorded activity, calendar, goal, and stats. Produce a Markdown response with exactly five sections separated by ## headings, in this exact order: Truth headline, Today's story, What held, What fragmented, Tomorrow's first 90. After the last section, emit a code-fenced JSON block containing the structured tail described below.

Voice constraints (non-negotiable):
- Lead with the truth, not the win. The day's data determines the headline's tone; the structure is invariant.
- Use direct, factual language. Adults can interpret numbers; do not over-explain.
- Never use these words in user-facing copy: should, failed, missed, wasted, drifted, off-track, skipped, behind, slipping, broken streak, lost focus, gave up, fell off, neglected, ignored.
- Prefer this vocabulary instead: returned, restarted, kept, partial, did not start, came back to, found your way to, stretches of focus, longest, you said, you've done.
- Do not interpret fragmentation as a character signal. Name the mechanism only.
- Do not connect any specific gap to a goal outcome.
- Do not use the word "but" to pivot from a positive to a negative.
- Forward-look in section 5. Never backward-grade.

The "What fragmented" section is the riskiest. Name the fragmentation pattern as a factual observation, the way a coach reviewing film names what happened on a play. You are describing a mechanism, not assigning a grade. Identify the specific switch pattern, the specific partial event, or the specific time window where attention split — and stop. Do not interpret it as a character signal. Do not connect it to a goal outcome. Do not use the word "but" to pivot from a positive. The reader already knows it didn't go how they wanted; your job is to make the mechanism visible so they can see it tomorrow, not to deliver a verdict on today. Two sentences maximum. If you cannot name the fragmentation in one specific concrete pattern, write one sentence saying the day was diffuse without a single dominant fragmentation signature.

For "Tomorrow's first 90": give a literal 90-minute block. Start time as HH:MM, single target (one project or task), and reference any calendar event that supports it (e.g., "after your 9am standup") or competes with it (e.g., "before your 11am Jackie call"). Be concrete. The reader needs a thing to walk toward at the start of tomorrow, not a feeling.

Output the structured tail as a code-fenced JSON object with these exact keys:
- day_shape: one of "diffuse" | "anchored" | "fragmented_bursts" | "stretched_focus" | "rest"
- dominant_fragmentation_pattern: one of "morning_drift" | "afternoon_slip" | "calendar_collision" | "context_thrash" | "none"
- tomorrow_first_90: object with start_local (HH:MM), target (string), supporting_event_id (string|null), competing_event_id (string|null)

If the user worked less than 30 minutes total (focused + elsewhere), the day_shape is "rest" and the brief should be shorter, kinder, and end at "Tomorrow's first 90" without dwelling on fragmentation.
```

The prompt version is stored in the `daily_briefs.prompt_version` column so future prompt revisions can be A/B compared.

## 6. Input payload to Claude

The user message to Claude is a single JSON object with this shape (TypeScript pseudo-types):

```typescript
interface BriefInputPayload {
  date: string;                              // YYYY-MM-DD local
  workHours: { start: string; end: string; enabled: boolean; weekendsActive: boolean };
  stats: DailyStatsDTO;                      // existing Phase 2a type
  projectBreakdown: ProjectBreakdownDTO[];   // top 5 by totalMs
  calendarEvents: Array<{
    id: string;
    title: string;
    startTimeMs: number;
    endTimeMs: number;
    projectLabel: string | null;
    status: 'kept' | 'partial' | 'did-not-start';
    overlapMs: number;
  }>;
  goal: WeeklyGoalDTO | null;
  goalProgressMsThisWeek: number;            // computed from sessions over the last 7 days matching goal.projectLabel
  focusBlocksDetailed: Array<{               // sessions where kind='work' AND effective >= 20min
    projectLabel: string;
    durationMs: number;
    startTime: number;
  }>;
  longestBlock: DailyStatsDTO['longestBlock'];
}
```

This is pre-aggregated. Raw 692-row session dumps NEVER leave the local machine. Typical payload size: 2-5k input tokens.

## 7. UI surfaces

### 7.1 Brief tab (new top-level tab)

Tab order: `Today | Brief | Projects | Exclusions | Schedule` (5 tabs).

**Layout:**

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Header: "Today, Wed May 27"                 │
│  [Generate brief] button (disabled if no key)│
│                                              │
│  ┌── Today's brief card ──────────────────┐  │
│  │ ## Truth headline                       │ │
│  │ <markdown rendered>                     │ │
│  │ ## Today's story                        │ │
│  │ ...                                     │ │
│  │ Footer: "Generated 5:43pm · Sonnet 4.5 │ │
│  │ · 4,231 in + 412 out tokens · 1 of 2   │ │
│  │ regens used. [Regenerate]"              │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                              │
│  ── Past briefs ──                           │
│  May 26 · 3 hours 12 minutes focused…  [▸]   │
│  May 25 · 0 hours 47 minutes focused…  [▸]   │
│  May 24 · 4 hours 6 minutes focused…   [▸]   │
│  ...                                         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Today's card** is always present. Its content is either (a) the generated brief, (b) the empty state, or (c) the no-key state.
- **Past briefs** is a flat date list with month dividers (`May 2026`, `April 2026`) appearing inline as the user scrolls.
- **Click on a past brief row** expands it inline (no navigation). Click again to collapse.
- **Streaming UX:** when a generation is in flight, the brief area shows the headline as soon as Claude emits it, then each subsequent section as it streams. A subtle pulsing cursor at the end-of-stream indicates "still arriving."
- **Per-brief footer** shows: generation timestamp, model used, token counts, regen status.

Add a new card below the existing Google Calendar card:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Anthropic API                                │
│ Your Anthropic API key powers the Daily      │
│ Brief. Stored locally via Electron safeStorage│

│                                              │
│ API key:    [sk-ant-api03-...     ] [Save]   │
│ Model:      [Sonnet 4.5      ▼]              │
│                                              │
│ [Test connection]                            │
│                                              │
│ ⚠ Connection failed: <error message>         │
│   (or)                                       │
│ ✓ Connected. Test brief generation cost:     │
│   ~$0.03 per brief.                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Model options use Anthropic's published model identifiers. The implementer MUST look up the current model IDs at implementation time from https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/models and store them in a `MODEL_IDS` constant in `src/main/anthropic/models.ts`. The UI labels stay stable: "Sonnet 4.5" (default), "Haiku 4.5 — faster, cheaper", "Opus 4.5 — slowest, smartest".

Test connection: a single minimal API call (`max_tokens: 1`) that validates the key and selected model without generating a real brief.

## 8. Data model

### 8.1 Migration `006_daily_briefs.sql`

```sql
CREATE TABLE daily_briefs (
  date TEXT PRIMARY KEY,             -- YYYY-MM-DD local
  generated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- Unix ms of most recent generation
  generation_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  model TEXT NOT NULL,
  prompt_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  input_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL,
  output_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL,

  -- Parsed sections
  headline TEXT NOT NULL,
  story TEXT NOT NULL,
  what_held TEXT NOT NULL,
  what_fragmented TEXT NOT NULL,
  tomorrow_first_90 TEXT NOT NULL,

  -- Raw Markdown (full response)
  raw_markdown TEXT NOT NULL,

  -- Parsed structured tail (JSON string, may be NULL on persistent parse failure)
  structured_tail TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX idx_daily_briefs_generated_at ON daily_briefs(generated_at DESC);
```

### 8.2 electron-store additions to `Prefs`

```typescript
type Prefs = {
  // ... existing fields ...
  anthropic: {
    apiKey?: string;          // safeStorage-encrypted base64
    model: string;            // 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20251022' default
  };
};
```

Default model: the Sonnet 4.5 model ID from `MODEL_IDS.sonnet`. Stored unencrypted (it's a public identifier).

## 9. IPC contract additions

```typescript
// Channels
BRIEF_TODAY:        'brief:today';            // returns DailyBriefDTO | null
BRIEF_LIST_PAST:    'brief:list_past';        // returns DailyBriefDTO[] (paginated, default 30)
BRIEF_GENERATE:     'brief:generate';         // streams chunks back via BRIEF_STREAM
BRIEF_STREAM:       'brief:stream';           // server-to-renderer streaming channel
BRIEF_REGEN_COUNT:  'brief:regen_count';      // returns { used: number; cap: number }
ANTHROPIC_GET_STATUS:    'anthropic:status';      // returns { hasKey: boolean; model: string }
ANTHROPIC_SET_KEY:       'anthropic:set_key';     // saves + encrypts via safeStorage
ANTHROPIC_SET_MODEL:     'anthropic:set_model';   // updates Prefs.anthropic.model
ANTHROPIC_TEST:          'anthropic:test';        // returns { ok: boolean; error?: string }
ANTHROPIC_CLEAR_KEY:     'anthropic:clear_key';   // removes stored key
```

### 9.1 DailyBriefDTO

```typescript
interface DailyBriefDTO {
  date: string;
  generatedAt: number;
  generationCount: number;
  model: string;
  promptVersion: string;
  inputTokens: number;
  outputTokens: number;
  headline: string;
  story: string;
  whatHeld: string;
  whatFragmented: string;
  tomorrowFirst90: string;
  rawMarkdown: string;
  structuredTail: StructuredTail | null;
}

interface StructuredTail {
  dayShape: 'diffuse' | 'anchored' | 'fragmented_bursts' | 'stretched_focus' | 'rest';
  dominantFragmentationPattern: 'morning_drift' | 'afternoon_slip' | 'calendar_collision' | 'context_thrash' | 'none';
  tomorrowFirst90: {
    startLocal: string;
    target: string;
    supportingEventId: string | null;
    competingEventId: string | null;
  };
}
```

### 9.2 Streaming protocol

`BRIEF_GENERATE` does NOT return the brief. It returns a generation-id and starts streaming chunks on `BRIEF_STREAM`. Each chunk is:

```typescript
type BriefStreamEvent =
  | { kind: 'text_delta'; generationId: string; delta: string }
  | { kind: 'section_complete'; generationId: string; section: 'headline' | 'story' | 'what_held' | 'what_fragmented' | 'tomorrow_first_90' }
  | { kind: 'done'; generationId: string; brief: DailyBriefDTO }
  | { kind: 'error'; generationId: string; message: string; retryable: boolean };
```

The renderer subscribes to `BRIEF_STREAM` filtered by `generationId`. On `done`, the cached brief is committed and the streaming UI swaps to the static render. On `error`, the error message is shown with a Retry button (which calls `BRIEF_GENERATE` again).

---

## 10. Banned-vocab gating

Two layers:

1. **System prompt** lists the banned words explicitly (see §5).
2. **Post-generation regex scan** runs against the parsed sections AFTER the stream completes. If any banned word is matched on a word boundary, the brief is **rejected and regenerated automatically** (without consuming a user-visible regen credit). System prompt is augmented with: `"Your previous response contained the banned word '<word>'. Regenerate without that word."`

Maximum 3 automatic regens for banned-vocab violations. After 3, the brief is stored with a warning footer: `"⚠ This brief contained vocabulary outside Remirror's tone constraints. Showing it anyway — let us know if you want it rewritten."` plus a manual rewrite button.

The regex MUST use word boundaries (`\b<word>\b`, case-insensitive). The full banned list is the canonical one from `CRYSTALLIZED-CONTEXT-adhd-design-frame.md` §banned-vocabulary, deduplicated and stored in `src/main/copy/banned-vocab.ts` for sharing between the Phase 2a test and Phase 4 gate.

---

## 11. Error handling

| Failure | Behavior |
|---|---|
| No API key | Empty state with deep-link to Settings. No generation attempt. |
| API key invalid (401) | Error inline + "Update your API key in Settings →" deep-link. |
| API rate limit (429) | Error inline + "Retrying in N seconds…" with exponential backoff (1s, 5s, 30s). 3 attempts. |
| Network failure | Error inline + Retry button. No backoff (user is interactive). |
| Anthropic 500/503 | Same as rate limit (exponential backoff). |
| Malformed Markdown (missing sections) | Auto-regenerate with stricter prompt. Max 3 attempts. After that, store raw and surface a "Couldn't parse — view raw" affordance. |
| Malformed structured tail | Auto-regenerate. Max 3 attempts. After that, store with `structured_tail = NULL`, log warning. |
| Banned-vocab violation | Auto-regenerate (see §10). Max 3 attempts. |
| Stream interrupted mid-flight | Partial discarded. Error inline + Retry button. No DB write. |

All errors are logged via electron-log. The user sees a clean message; the developer sees the full Anthropic response body.

## 12. Cost transparency

- **Per-brief footer:** "Generated 5:43pm · Sonnet 4.5 · 4,231 in + 412 out tokens"
- **Settings card:** "Test brief generation cost: ~$0.03 per brief" (model-dependent estimate)
- **No monthly aggregation in v1.** Defer to v0.4.x if users ask.

Cost estimates per model (typical 5k in + 600 out brief, as of 2026-05-27 pricing):
- Haiku 4.5: ~$0.005
- Sonnet 4.5: ~$0.025
- Opus 4.5: ~$0.10

Estimates are static strings in the UI — no live API price-discovery in v1.

## 13. Privacy copy

Shown verbatim in three places: Brief tab empty state, Schedule tab Anthropic API card, and a `?` tooltip on the Generate button.

> Your data stays on this machine except when you generate a brief. At that moment, the day's aggregated stats — focus blocks, switches, calendar adherence, project breakdown, goal progress — are sent to the Anthropic API using your key. Anthropic does not train on API traffic by default. No data is logged, proxied, or shared with Remirror servers (there are no Remirror servers).

The exact list of data fields sent is enumerated in §6 above and reproduced under a `?` tooltip in the Brief tab footer.

## 14. Testing strategy

### 14.1 Unit tests (Vitest)

- `tests/copy/banned-vocab.test.ts` — extend to cover §5's bad-day exemplar (zero violations)
- `tests/brief/assemble-payload.test.ts` — given fixture DB rows + work hours + calendar, the assembled payload matches expected shape
- `tests/brief/parse-markdown.test.ts` — given a streamed Markdown sample, the section parser extracts five sections correctly
- `tests/brief/parse-structured-tail.test.ts` — given a Markdown sample with code-fenced JSON, the tail parses; given malformed JSON, parser returns null
- `tests/brief/regen-cap.test.ts` — incrementing the generation_count past 3 (1 initial + 2 regens) disables the regenerate button

### 14.2 Integration tests (Vitest, no live API)

Mock the Anthropic SDK at the IPC boundary. The streaming protocol is tested by feeding pre-recorded SSE-like chunks and asserting renderer state transitions.

### 14.3 Live API tests (gated, not run in CI)

A separate `npm run test:live` invokes one real generation against the developer's own key. Asserts: a brief is produced, all five sections are non-empty, structured tail parses, banned-vocab scan is clean. Costs ~$0.03 per run. NOT in the default `npm test` flow.

## 15. Acceptance criteria (manual walkthrough)

1. ✅ Brief tab appears in the top tab bar between Today and Projects.
2. ✅ With no API key, Brief tab shows the empty-state + deep-link to Settings → Anthropic API.
3. ✅ Schedule tab shows the Anthropic API card with key field + model picker + Test button.
4. ✅ Pasting an invalid API key and clicking Test surfaces the error inline.
5. ✅ Pasting a valid API key + clicking Test surfaces a green ✓ + estimated cost.
6. ✅ Clicking Generate (with valid key) starts a stream. Text appears section-by-section in <2 seconds to first token.
7. ✅ Generated brief renders five sections with `## ` headings.
8. ✅ Brief footer shows generation time, model, token counts, regen status.
9. ✅ Regenerating once shows "1 of 2 regens used." Regenerating again shows the button disabled and the "This is the brief. Sit with it." line.
10. ✅ Past briefs list shows yesterday's brief (if one exists), with month dividers when scrolling.
11. ✅ Clicking a past brief expands it inline.
12. ✅ The bad-day exemplar from §4.3 passes the banned-vocab linter.
13. ✅ Banned-vocab violations in Claude's output trigger automatic regeneration (visible in logs).
14. ✅ Tests: 100+ unit/integration tests pass.

## 16. Out of scope (deferred)

- **Auto-fire trigger** (deferred to v0.4.x — see §2)
- **Monthly cost aggregation** (deferred to v0.4.x)
- **Brief sharing / export** (deferred — would require copy review)
- **Brief editing post-generation** (intentionally not shipped — user shouldn't be able to revise their own mirror)
- **Multi-model brief comparison** (deferred — would multiply costs)
- **Push notifications when brief is ready** (no auto-fire = no notification need)
- **Phase 5 weekly mirror UI** — Phase 5's own work; this spec only ensures Phase 4 outputs the structured tail that Phase 5 will consume.

## 17. Schema for `daily_briefs` table — verification queries

To verify the schema works end-to-end, the following queries should run cleanly post-migration:

```sql
-- Insert a sample brief
INSERT INTO daily_briefs (date, generated_at, generation_count, model, prompt_version,
  input_tokens, output_tokens, headline, story, what_held, what_fragmented,
  tomorrow_first_90, raw_markdown, structured_tail)
VALUES ('2026-05-27', 1748390123000, 1, '<sonnet-4-5-model-id>', 'v1.0',
  4231, 412, 'sample headline', 'sample story', 'sample held',
  'sample fragmented', 'sample tomorrow', '## headline\n...', NULL);

-- Read it back
SELECT * FROM daily_briefs WHERE date = '2026-05-27';

-- Bump regen count
UPDATE daily_briefs SET generation_count = generation_count + 1 WHERE date = '2026-05-27';

-- List past briefs
SELECT date, generated_at, headline FROM daily_briefs ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 30;
```

This spec is the source of truth for what Phase 4 ships and why.
